pass_a_gloss: And the third, setting the pains at nothing and through love toward God trampling them, being asked the tongue quickly put it forward and stretched forth the hands with good courage; and he said: having left these behind because of the laws of God I hope to get them back from God of such a sort as God would give back to the athletes of piety toward himself. Likewise also the fourth was tortured, carrying the outrages and saying that it is preferable, changing away from humans, to look for the hopes from God and to be raised by him, a raising which the tyrant will not rise with; for not to life but to reproach and to shame eternal will he rise. Next he outraged the fifth, who, looking at Antiochus, reproached him with the perishable, not cutting back his arrogance, he supposing the tyranny in few days to be a great authority. And he declared, being even in these, that the nation was not abandoned by God, who was all but already about to torture Antiochus and his seed. After this one the sixth, having come near dying, said: do not be misled; we, paying penalties on behalf of our sins, in order that in the toils we be cleansed, willingly suffer these things. And he was telling him that indeed he must not suppose he will be guiltless attempting to fight God; for a God-fighter is the one fighting those made gods by the Word.
pass_b_english: The third, too, counted his pains as nothing and trampled on them for love of God. “When asked for his tongue, he quickly put it out, and he boldly stretched out his hands” (2 Maccabees 7:10), and he said: “I give these up for the sake of God's laws, and I hope to receive them back from God in such a form as God would give back to those who contend in godliness toward him.”

In the same way the fourth was tortured, bearing the torments and saying that it is better, when departing this life at the hands of men, to wait for the hopes that come from God and to be raised up by him, with a resurrection to which the tyrant will not rise. For he will rise not “to life” (2 Maccabees 7:14) but to reproach and to everlasting shame (Daniel 12:2).

Next he tormented the fifth, who looked straight at Antiochus and reproached him with being mortal, since he did not curb his arrogance but thought a tyranny of a few days to be great power. Even in these torments he declared that his nation had not been “forsaken” by God, who was very soon to torment Antiochus “and his seed” (2 Maccabees 7:16-17).

After him the sixth, at the point of death, said: “Do not deceive yourself. We are paying the penalty for our own sins, so that we may be cleansed in our pains, and we suffer these things willingly” (2 Maccabees 7:18). And he told him that he must not think he would go unpunished when he set himself “to fight against God” (2 Maccabees 7:19). For whoever fights against those made divine by the Word is a fighter against God.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 25); the old English was a digest built from 2 Maccabees 7:10-19 in King James wording ('These I had from heaven ... abide a little and see his great power'), added an exclamation ('O noble exchange') not in the Greek, and dropped Origen's own lines: the third's hope to receive his limbs back as God gives to his athletes, the fourth's 'reproach and everlasting shame', the fifth's rebuke of a 'tyranny of a few days', and the sixth's 'that we may be cleansed in our pains'.
Read τοῦ (θεοῦ) ὅσον οὐδέπω ... βασανίσοντος: 'by God, who was very soon to torment Antiochus'.

choices.issue: μὴ κολούων αὐτοῦ τὴν ὑπερηφανίαν (variants κολλούων, Wettstein καλλύνων, Delarue κολοῖον)
choices.choice: Grammatically the participle belongs to the fifth brother, but the sense (with νομίζοντος, of Antiochus) is the king's unchecked arrogance; rendered 'since he did not curb his arrogance' and flagged in translator_notes.
ἀπό taken of the agent, as in 2 Macc 7:14 (ὑπ᾽ ἀνθρώπων): 'when departing this life at the hands of men'.
Read μὴ πλανῶ, ταῦτα πάσχομεν, εἰς ζωήν.
'those made divine by the Word' (deification), kept literally; Wettstein's conjecture θεοπειθέσι is rejected by Koetschau.

source_text: Καὶ ὃ τρίτος δὲ ἐν οὐδενὶ τὰς ἀλγηδόνας τιϑέμενος καὶ διὰ τὴν πρὸς τὸν ϑεὸν ἀγάπην καταπατῶν αὐτὰς ,τὴν γλῶσσαν αἰτηϑεὶς ταχέως προέβαλε καὶ τὰς χεῖρας εὐθαρσῶς προέτεινεν" εἶπε re’ διὰ τοὺς τοῦ ϑεοῦ νόμους ταῦτα καταλιπὼν ἐλπίζω αὐτὰ ἀπὸ ϑεοῦ χομίσασϑαι τοιαῦτα, οἷα ἂν ἀποδῴη ϑεὸς τοῖς τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν εὐσεβείας ἀϑληταῖς. ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ ὃ τέταρτος ἐβασανίζετο τὰς αἰχίας φέρων καὶ λέγων ὅτι: αἱρετὸν μεταλλάσσοντας ἀπ᾿ ἀνϑρώπων τὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ ϑεοῦ προσδοχᾶν ἐλπίδας καὶ ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἀναστήσεσϑαι" ἀνάστασιν, ἣν οὐκ ἀναστήσεται 6 τύραννος" οὐ γὰρ „els ζωὴν" ἀλλὰ εἰς ὀνειδισμὸν καὶ εἰς αἰσχύνην αἰώνιον ἀναστήσεται. ἑξῆς τὸν πέμπτον ἠχίσατο, ὃς ἐνιδὼν τῷ ᾿Αντιόχῳ ὠνείδισεν αὐτῷ τὸ φϑαρτὸν μὴ κολούων αὐτοῦ τὴν ὑπερηφανίαν, νομίζοντος μεγάλην εἶναι ἐξουσίαν τὴν ἐν ὀλίγαις ἡμέραις τυραννίδα. ἔφασκε δὲ καὶ ἐν τούτοις ὧν τὸ ἔϑνος μὴ ,χαταλελεῖφϑαι" ὑπὸ ϑεοῦ τοῖ ὅσον οὐδέπω τὸν ᾿Αντίοχον ,καὶ τὸ σπέρμα" αὐτοῦ βασανίσοντος. μετὰ τοῦτον ὁ ἕχτος πρὸς τῷ ἀποϑνήσχειν γενόμενος «μὴ πλαvo“, εἶπεν. ἡμεῖς ὑπὲρ ἡμετέρων ἁμαρτημάτων δίκας τίνοντες, ἵν ἐν τοῖς πόνοις καϑαρισϑῶμεν, ἑκουσίως „radra πάσχομεν". ἔλεγέ τε αὐτῷ, ὡὑς ἄρα οὐ χρὴ νομίζειν αὐτὸν ἀϑῷον ἔσεσϑαι ,ϑεομαχεῖν" ἐπιχειροῦντα- ϑεομάχος γὰρ ὃ τοῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ λόγου ϑεοποιηϑεῖσι μαχόμενος.
